generation_notes: Revised to exactly 18 candidate seed sequences and repaired prior review findings by using only evidence IDs present in the supplied sources, converting the corpus to consistent CS104-style APDUs where transport framing is needed, fixing deterministic length relations, correcting the local-command CoT mismatch, removing unsupported unknown-type 127 use as a primary boundary seed, and reducing near-duplicate minimal TypeID-1 CoT-only seeds by replacing several with structurally distinct TypeIDs and system-command variants. All framed messages preserve the documented IEC 60870-5-104 start byte 0x68, explicit APDU length, 4-byte APCI control field, then ASDU fields in documented order. Because the supplied protocol sources make ASDU field sizing configurable, the seeds intentionally follow one internally consistent and mutation-friendly profile assumption used repeatedly in the local documentation and issue material: 2-octet cause_of_transmission, 2-octet common_address, and 3-octet information_object_address in little-endian form when multi-octet. Issue-guided analogues stay close to the cited parser-sensitive paths, especially TypeID 104 C_TS_NA_1 and address-handling logic, while avoiding any exact published crash payloads, oversize VSQ claims, truncated IOA fields, or mismatched APDU lengths.

global_feedback: The library shows good intent: framing is consistent at the CS104 APDU level, lengths mostly match, and the corpus avoids replaying the published crash payloads.
The strongest seeds are the canonical C_SC_NA_1 baseline, the stateful C_IC_NA_1 sequence, and the two TypeID 104 analogues; these are structurally complete and likely to reach useful parser paths.

A major weakness is semantic validity of several object payloads. The supplied sources only explicitly describe object-specific fields for C_SC_NA_1 and give generic ASDU/header rules; several other TypeIDs are asserted with minimal bodies that are not supported by the provided object templates and are unlikely to be valid requests.

Multiple seeds use cause-of-transmission values such as 44-47 as if they were ordinary fuzzable request seeds. Those values are error/report causes, not normal initiating causes, so they are weak as initial coverage seeds and may be dropped early on semantic checks.

Several monitoring/system-command seeds rely on guessed one-byte object payloads or IOA-only bodies without source-backed object layouts. This lowers confidence that they will survive beyond shallow parsing.
There is too much concentration on C_SC_NA_1 with mostly CoT/address variation. For a desired selected count of 12, the current library has more than six marginal variants competing for slots.
Issue enhancement is used appropriately in spirit: the TypeID 104 seeds preserve the parser-sensitive structure while avoiding oversized VSQ/body mismatches and avoiding the exact GHSA PoC.

The best revision path is to keep the strong framed/stateful/issue-guided seeds, drop weak CoT-only carrier variants, and replace them with source-backed operations whose object payloads are actually documented or can be made confidently complete.

Section: Message Templates
Template: ASDU
- Field: type_id
  Description: Protocol field 'type_id'. Layer: asdu. Role: type. Type: enum. Range: [1, 127]. Inferred-from: wire. Binding-strength: direct_byte_parse. Evidence-type: offset.
  Length: 8 bits
  Implementation constraints: must be one of the IEC 60870-5-101/104 valid TypeID values (1..127)
- Field: vsq
  Description: Protocol field 'vsq'. Layer: asdu. Role: control. Type: uint8. Constraints: 7-bit count 1..127, MSB=1 indicates sequence format, MSB=0 indicates non-sequence format. Range: [0, 127]. Inferred-from: wire. Binding-strength: direct_byte_parse. Evidence-type: mask.
  Length: 8 bits
  Implementation constraints: mask 0x7f applied to extract count, mask 0x80 applied to extract flag, bit-7 encodes format flag, bits 0-6 encode element count
- Field: cause_of_transmission
  Description: Protocol field 'cause_of_transmission'. Layer: asdu. Role: cause. Type: uint8|uint16. Constraints: parameters->sizeOfCOT determines 1 or 2 octets, bit-7 is P/N bit, bit-6 is T bit. Range: [0, 65535]. Inferred-from: wire. Binding-strength: direct_byte_parse. Evidence-type: offset|mask|length_check.
  Length: 8|16 bits
  Implementation constraints: sizeOfCOT in parameters object, sizeOfCOT set by standard configuration
- Field: common_address
  Description: Protocol field 'common_address'. Layer: asdu. Role: address. Type: uint8|uint16. Constraints: size determined by CS101_AppLayerParameters.sizeOfCA (1 or 2), little-endian byte order for 2-byte case. Range: [0, 65535]. Inferred-from: wire. Binding-strength: direct_byte_parse. Evidence-type: offset.
  Length: 8|16 bits
  Implementation constraints: must be placed immediately after COT field, sizeOfCA is fixed for a single link/connection
- Field: information_object_address

Issue: GHSA-G3W7-X5RX-83XM
Summary: In lib60870-C v2.4.0, parsing a crafted IEC 60870-5-104 I-frame for TypeID 104 (C_TS_NA_1) with a VSQ/object count larger than the ASDU body can hold can make TestCommand_getFromBuffer read 1 byte past the end of the heap-allocated message buffer. The immediate cause is that TestCommand_getFromBuffer calls InformationObject_ParseObjectAddress(msg, startIndex), and that helper has no msgSize parameter, so startIndex cannot be checked against the end of the buffer. The demonstrated impact is a heap out-of-bounds read detected under AddressSanitizer. The document additionally argues that roughly 150 *_getFromBuffer functions in cs101_information_objects.c share the same structural limitation, but the demonstrated crash here is in TestCommand_getFromBuffer.
Reproduce: Prerequisite/build setup: lib60870-C v2.4.0 fuzzed with LibFuzzer and AddressSanitizer. Provide the parser with a crafted IEC 60870-5-104 I-frame targeting TypeID 104 (C_TS_NA_1) whose VSQ/object count claims more objects than the ASDU body actually contains. When parsing reaches TestCommand_getFromBuffer, it calls InformationObject_ParseObjectAddress(msg, startIndex); because no message-size check is available there, startIndex advances past the heap allocation. Expected result: AddressSanitizer reports a 1-byte heap-buffer-over-read. The source also shows a 16-byte PoC hex string, 68 0e 00 00 eb 00 68 06 15 24 00 04 00 00 80 00, but notes uncertainty about the byte-level TypeID/offset interpretation.

global_feedback: The library is generally conservative and avoids obvious crash-payload replay, which is good for initial seeds.
A major strength is consistent use of complete field ordering inside the ASDU and mostly coherent IEC 104 outer framing for the framed seeds.

The weakest area is protocol certainty: several seeds assume 2-octet COT, 2-octet CA, and 3-octet IOA without a source that fully fixes those parameters for the intended target profile, and one framed seed has an incorrect stated length relation.
The corpus overuses a very small minimal shape, especially TypeID 1 one-object CS104 I-frames that differ only in cause of transmission; this limits structural diversity.
Issue-guided analogues are mostly safe, but some do not actually target the issue-referenced TypeID/path closely enough and instead only preserve generic framing.
Stateful coverage is underdeveloped: only one multi-message sequence is present, and it is ASDU-only while many other seeds are CS104-framed, reducing consistency.

Deterministic validator findings show widespread invalid or removed evidence references; this does not break the wire data directly but does reduce confidence in grounding, especially for seeds 007 and 008 which are absent and for several kept seeds whose rationale depends on removed evidence.
For a desired final set of 12, the current library has enough candidates, but several should be revised or deprioritized so the final selection is not dominated by near-duplicate COT-only variants.

global_feedback: The library shows good intent: framing is consistent at the CS104 APDU level, lengths mostly match, and the corpus avoids replaying the published crash payloads.
The strongest seeds are the canonical C_SC_NA_1 baseline, the stateful C_IC_NA_1 sequence, and the two TypeID 104 analogues; these are structurally complete and likely to reach useful parser paths.

A major weakness is semantic validity of several object payloads. The supplied sources only explicitly describe object-specific fields for C_SC_NA_1 and give generic ASDU/header rules; several other TypeIDs are asserted with minimal bodies that are not supported by the provided object templates and are unlikely to be valid requests.

Multiple seeds use cause-of-transmission values such as 44-47 as if they were ordinary fuzzable request seeds. Those values are error/report causes, not normal initiating causes, so they are weak as initial coverage seeds and may be dropped early on semantic checks.

Several monitoring/system-command seeds rely on guessed one-byte object payloads or IOA-only bodies without source-backed object layouts. This lowers confidence that they will survive beyond shallow parsing.
There is too much concentration on C_SC_NA_1 with mostly CoT/address variation. For a desired selected count of 12, the current library has more than six marginal variants competing for slots.
Issue enhancement is used appropriately in spirit: the TypeID 104 seeds preserve the parser-sensitive structure while avoiding oversized VSQ/body mismatches and avoiding the exact GHSA PoC.

The best revision path is to keep the strong framed/stateful/issue-guided seeds, drop weak CoT-only carrier variants, and replace them with source-backed operations whose object payloads are actually documented or can be made confidently complete.

Need at least one well-supported unknown-cause/address handling seed that is valid in role and semantics, not just by framing.
Need replacement seeds for C_RD_NA_1, C_CS_NA_1, and C_RP_NA_1 unless their object-specific payload requirements can be confirmed.
Need better boundary coverage around VSQ/count with explicitly supported object templates; current sequence-form seeds rely on ambiguous assumptions.
Need broader type coverage from documented control-direction types such as C_DC_NA_1, C_RC_NA_1, or parameter/file-transfer types only if full object bodies can be validated from sources.

export_metadata.note: concat preserves model-produced protocol bytes and adds no external length prefix. Message boundaries remain available in sequence.json and the per-message frame files.
